Labrador Retrievers have proven to have a high success rate at becoming guide dogs. A study published in 2006, tested the suitability of four different breeds (Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, Labrador Retriever/Golden Retriever Mix, and German Shepherds) as guide dogs. In this experiment, German Shepherds had the highest chance of not completing it. Labrador Retrievers and the Labrador Retriever/Golden Retriever Crossbreeds had the highest success rate. However, German Shepherds and Golden Retrievers had a higher success rate after going through longer training than the training required for Labrador Retrievers.[[34]](#cite_note-35)[[35]](#cite_note-36)

The Labrador Retriever is a gun dog bred to retrieve on land and water.[[36]](#cite_note-magazine-37) As a dog specially bred for water retrieving, the Labrador has developed various traits for this job. For retrieving the Labrador Retriever has a [soft mouth](/wiki/Bite_inhibition "Bite inhibition"), a trait that allows it to carry game and waterfowl without damaging it.[[37]](#cite_note-Journal-38) And for swimming, the Labrador is aided by fully webbed paws, an otter-like tail, and a waterproof coat.[[38]](#cite_note-Eight-39)

The high intelligence, initiative and self-direction of Labradors in working roles is exemplified by dogs such as [Endal](/wiki/Endal "Endal"), who was trained to, if need be, put his human who uses a wheelchair in the recovery position, cover him with a blanket, and activate an emergency phone.[[39]](#cite_note-40) A number of Labradors have also been taught to assist their owner in removing money and credit cards from [ATMs](/wiki/Automated_teller_machine "Automated teller machine") with prior training.[[40]](#cite_note-41)

Milan's main rivalry is with its neighbour club, [Inter Milan](/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan"). Both clubs meet in the widely anticipated [Derby della Madonnina](/wiki/Derby_della_Madonnina "Derby della Madonnina") twice every Serie A season. The name of the derby refers to the [Blessed Virgin Mary](/wiki/Blessed_Virgin_Mary "Blessed Virgin Mary"), whose statue atop the [Milan Cathedral](/wiki/Milan_Cathedral "Milan Cathedral") is one of the city's main attractions. The first match was held in the final of the Chiasso Cup of 1908, a football tournament played in Canton Ticino, Switzerland, on 18 October of that year; the Rossoneri won 2–1.[[93]](#cite_note-96) The rivalry reached its highest point in the 1960s, when the two clubs dominated the scene both domestically and internationally. In Italy they cumulatively won five Serie A titles, while internationally they collected four European cups. On the bench it showcased the clash of two different approaches to [Catenaccio](/wiki/Catenaccio "Catenaccio") by the two managers: [Nereo Rocco](/wiki/Nereo_Rocco "Nereo Rocco") for Milan and [Helenio Herrera](/wiki/Helenio_Herrera "Helenio Herrera") for Inter. Mercury has the most [eccentric](/wiki/Orbital_eccentricity "Orbital eccentricity") orbit of all the planets in the Solar System; its eccentricity is 0.21 with its distance from the Sun ranging from 46,000,000 to 70,000,000 km (29,000,000 to 43,000,000 mi). It takes 87.969 Earth days to complete an orbit. The diagram illustrates the effects of the eccentricity, showing Mercury's orbit overlaid with a circular orbit having the same [semi-major axis](/wiki/Semi-major_axis "Semi-major axis"). Mercury's higher velocity when it is near perihelion is clear from the greater distance it covers in each 5-day interval. In the diagram, the varying distance of Mercury to the Sun is represented by the size of the planet, which is inversely proportional to Mercury's distance from the Sun.

This varying distance to the Sun leads to Mercury's surface being flexed by [tidal bulges](/wiki/Tidal_bulge "Tidal bulge") raised by the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") that are about 17 times stronger than the Moon's on Earth.[[110]](#cite_note-110) Combined with a 3:2 [spin–orbit resonance](#Spin-orbit_resonance) of the planet's rotation around its axis, it also results in complex variations of the surface temperature.[[28]](#cite_note-strom-28) The resonance makes a single [solar day](/wiki/Solar_day "Solar day") (the length between two [meridian](/wiki/Meridian_(astronomy) "Meridian (astronomy)") transits of the Sun) on Mercury last exactly two Mercury years, or about 176 Earth days.[[111]](#cite_note-compare-111)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Taj_Mahal-10_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Taj_Mahal-10_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Taj_Mahal-10_(cropped).jpg)

The Taj Mahal complex is situated on a platform on the banks of the [Yamuna](/wiki/Yamuna "Yamuna") River.

The Taj Mahal incorporates and expands on design traditions of [Indo-Islamic](/wiki/Indo-Islamic_architecture "Indo-Islamic architecture") and [Mughal architecture](/wiki/Mughal_architecture "Mughal architecture").[[20]](#cite_note-Arch-20) Inspirations for the building came from [Timurid](/wiki/Timurid_dynasty "Timurid dynasty") and [Mughal](/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire") buildings including the [Gur-e Amir](/wiki/Gur-e_Amir "Gur-e Amir") in [Samarkand](/wiki/Samarkand "Samarkand") (the tomb of [Timur](/wiki/Timur "Timur"), progenitor of the Mughal dynasty) and [Humayun's Tomb](/wiki/Humayun%27s_Tomb "Humayun's Tomb") in Delhi which inspired the [Charbagh](/wiki/Charbagh "Charbagh") gardens and [hasht-behesht](/wiki/Hasht-behesht_(architecture) "Hasht-behesht (architecture)") plan of the site.[[21]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaghtai1938146-21)[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKoch200685-88-22) The building complex employs symmetrical constructions with the usage of various shapes and symbols.[[20]](#cite_note-Arch-20) While the mausoleum is constructed of white [marble](/wiki/Marble "Marble") inlaid with [semi-precious stones](/wiki/Semi-precious_stones "Semi-precious stones"), red [sandstone](/wiki/Sandstone "Sandstone") was used for other buildings in the complex similar to the Mughal era buildings of the time.[[23]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECopplestone1963166-23) The entire complex sits on a platform measuring 300 metres (980 ft) in length and 8.7 metres (28.5 ft) in height on the banks of the [Yamuna river](/wiki/Yamuna_river "Yamuna river"). The platform is built with varying patterns of dark and light colored sandstone.[[24]](#cite_note-Arch2-24)

The first professional baseball team in Japan with later ties to NPB was founded by media mogul [Matsutarō Shōriki](/wiki/Matsutar%C5%8D_Sh%C5%8Driki "Matsutarō Shōriki") in late 1934 and called the [Dai Nippon Tokyo Yakyu Kurabu](/wiki/Dai_Nippon_Tokyo_Yakyu_Kurabu "Dai Nippon Tokyo Yakyu Kurabu") ("the Great Japan Tokyo Baseball Club"). After matching up with a team of visiting American All-Stars that included [Babe Ruth](/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth"), [Jimmie Foxx](/wiki/Jimmie_Foxx "Jimmie Foxx"), [Lou Gehrig](/wiki/Lou_Gehrig "Lou Gehrig"), and [Charlie Gehringer](/wiki/Charlie_Gehringer "Charlie Gehringer"), the team spent the 1935 season barnstorming in the U.S., winning 93 of 102 games against semi-pro and [Pacific Coast League](/wiki/Pacific_Coast_League "Pacific Coast League") teams. According to historian Joseph Reaves, "The only minor drawbacks to the team's popularity in the States were their [kanji](/wiki/Kanji "Kanji") characters and their cumbersome Japanese name. They rectified both by renaming themselves the [Tokyo Kyojin](/wiki/Tokyo_Kyojin "Tokyo Kyojin") ['Tokyo Giants'] and adopting a uniform identical to the [New York Giants](/wiki/New_York_Giants_(baseball_team) "New York Giants (baseball team)")..."[[11]](#cite_note-11)

From 1936 to 1950, [professional baseball in Japan](/wiki/Professional_baseball_in_Japan "Professional baseball in Japan") was played under the banner of the [Japanese Baseball League](/wiki/Japanese_Baseball_League "Japanese Baseball League") (JBL). The league's dominant team during this period was the [Tokyo Kyojin](/wiki/Tokyo_Kyojin "Tokyo Kyojin"), which won nine league championships, including six in a row from 1938 to 1943 (The team was officially renamed the [Yomiuri Giants](/wiki/Yomiuri_Giants "Yomiuri Giants") in 1947).

*The Tale of the Princess Kaguya* has been noted for its [feminist](/wiki/Feminism "Feminism") themes. Kaguya’s move to the capital and her father’s insistence that she adopt the life of a noblewoman run counter to her wishes, while her mother’s limited role in decision-making highlights the lack of female agency in the household. Yalcinkaya points to a [dream sequence](/wiki/Dream_sequence "Dream sequence") in which Kaguya breaks through a series of doors as a metaphor for the barriers imposed by family and society.[[26]](#cite_note-Yalcinkaya-27)

The film also critiques ideals of beauty and propriety during the [Heian period](/wiki/Heian_period "Heian period"). According to Monji, Kaguya’s training in court etiquette, which required her to suppress her emotions, amounts to a painful renunciation of humanity. Her decision to set impossible tasks for her suitors has further been read as a depiction of female resistance within a male-dominated hierarchy.[[27]](#cite_note-Monji-28)
